title: Make the coverage gate read jail_args and refuse a suite that dies partway
objective: Close the two review-found defects that let checks pass more easily than they should: is_covered() ignored the jail_args marker every other consumer reads, and bash's command hash cache made two 'tool is missing' assertions test the opposite of their names.
acceptance_criteria: is_covered() reads the jail_args file beside a suite's run_all.sh, the same marker ci_mirror.sh and shell-tests.yml consume, so a suite declares its own mounts in exactly one place.
A suite with no jail_args still gets the historical default binds, so nothing that passed before starts failing for lack of a marker.
A jail_args that is present but empty is a hard error, never a silent skip.
is_covered() passes --fail-on-case-error, so a suite that aborts partway fails the gate rather than being graded on the lines it reached before dying.
NEGATIVE CONTROL: stripping the binds a suite needs must make the gate exit non-zero. Before this change both the working and the broken configuration exited 0.
dot_resolver_install.sh, which is already off the allowlist, still clears the real gate afterwards -- the campaign's proof that 100% is reachable must survive the stricter check.
Every 'tool is missing' assertion genuinely hides the tool: removal clears bash's hash table via a shared _t_unstub helper.
No measured coverage figure moves as a result of either fix, and every existing assertion still passes.
shellcheck clean with no suppressions; all files within the 250-line cap.
out_of_scope: test_cco_state.sh's removal of beeper.orig: get_real_binary probes with [[ -f ]], which the hash cache does not affect.
test_aw_autostart.sh's removal of aw-qt: the assertion runs in a subshell via $status_script, so the parent shell's cache is irrelevant.
Arming check_shell_coverage.sh in any hook; that waits for allowlist-zero.
The kcov under-report, which is tracked separately in docs/shell-split-verification.md.
verifier: bash meta/scripts/check_shell_coverage.sh on dot_resolver_install.sh must exit 0; replacing that directory's jail_args with `--bind /etc` alone must make the same command exit non-zero, and restoring it must return exit 0 with an empty git diff --stat. Plus the features/lib runner under --fail-on-case-error reporting zero case failures, and all four features libs re-measured at their pre-change figures.
